description:
Project: KV cache compaction improvements (Serving Runtime Performance — Kernel + Scheduling)

Problem / motivation:
Redwood’s serving runtime relies heavily on the GPU KV cache for decoding efficiency. Under bursty traffic and mixed sequence-length distributions, the KV cache becomes fragmented (holes from completed/evicted sequences, uneven block utilization), which increases allocator/search overhead, raises the probability of expensive re-allocations, and causes bursty p95/p99 latency spikes. In some regions/pools this also increases OOM risk and forces conservative admission control, hurting throughput and customer SLOs.

Goals:
- Reduce KV cache memory fragmentation under real production mixes (prefill/decode interleaving, variable context lengths, multi-tenant pools).
- Reduce burst tail latencies attributable to KV cache allocation/eviction churn (target measurable p95/p99 improvements on internal perf suites and perf-canary).
- Provide a clear eviction/compaction strategy that is scheduler-aware (fairness, backpressure) and safe under concurrency.
- Improve observability: allocator/fragmentation metrics, compaction cost metrics, and per-request attribution to tail latency.
- Ship behind a runtime flag with safe incremental rollout (canary by region/pool), with clear rollback levers.

Non-goals:
- Rewriting the entire attention cache subsystem or changing model semantics.
- Long-horizon memory defragmentation across device resets (we focus on online compaction/eviction during runtime).
- Product/console UX changes beyond dashboards/alerts needed for safe rollout.

Scope / technical approach (expected):
- Introduce a compaction-capable allocator (e.g., block/page-based KV cache with movable segments) or a two-tier strategy (hot/cold segments) to reduce holes.
- Define eviction policy that cooperates with the scheduler (e.g., priority by request age, SLA class, tenant tier, or “likely-to-be-reused” prefix cache heuristics).
- Add compaction triggers and budgets: threshold-based (fragmentation ratio), time-based, and “on allocation failure” fallback.
- Implement safety constraints: compaction must respect in-flight kernels, stream synchronization, and must not regress average latency.
- Extend performance suite and canary checks to cover fragmentation + burst scenarios.

Stakeholders / teams:
- Engineering (Serving Runtime): Mateo Alvarez (VP Eng Runtime), Sofia Ivanova (Scheduling), Hiro Tanaka (Kernels), Noah Patel (runtime architecture), Omar El-Sayed & Samir Qureshi (KV cache/memory management), Marcus Reed/Rina Kobayashi (perf suite).
- SRE/Infra: Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes, Allison Grant (observability) for rollout, SLOs, and incident prevention.
- Product: Nikhil Sharma (Hosted API), Lauren Bishop (Dedicated) for customer impact prioritization and rollout expectations.

Milestones / timeline (hypothetical):
- Phase 0 (1–2 weeks): incident/data review, instrumentation, baseline fragmentation benchmarks; draft design.
- Phase 1 (2–4 weeks): implement allocator + metrics + feature flag; integrate initial eviction strategy.
- Phase 2 (2–3 weeks): scheduler integration, compaction triggers/budgets, regression testing; perf suite + perf-canary.
- Phase 3 (1–2 weeks): canary rollout (one region + one dedicated pool), dashboards/alerts, iterate.
- Phase 4 (1–2 weeks): broad rollout and documentation (runbooks, standards, release notes).

Key deliverables:
- Confluence design doc + ADRs for key tradeoffs.
- Linear project + execution tickets.
- GitHub PR series implementing allocator/eviction/metrics/tests.
- Dashboards/alerts and runbooks for monitoring + rollback.
- Support artifacts tying customer-reported tail latency to the fix (Jira, comms).

files.description: Primary design doc: fragmentation problem statement, proposed compaction/eviction architecture, data structures, concurrency model, scheduler integration points, performance expectations, testing strategy, and rollout plan (feature flag + canary).
ADR: choose KV cache allocation granularity (page/block size), whether blocks are movable, tradeoffs vs kernel complexity, and migration plan.
ADR: define compaction triggers (fragmentation ratio, allocation pressure) and compaction budget model (time/token budget) to protect median latency.
ADR: define eviction strategy and the explicit contract between scheduler and KV cache (priority classes, fairness constraints, overload behavior).
Runtime architecture page update: allocator internals, fragmentation definitions, new counters/telemetry, and how components (scheduler, prefix cache, kernels) interact.
Perf methodology doc: new benchmark scenarios (bursty arrivals, mixed lengths, multi-tenant), metrics (fragmentation ratio, compaction cost), and acceptance thresholds.
Step-by-step profiling guide: how to capture allocator stats, GPU memory snapshots, and correlate compaction events with p99 latency spikes.
Known issue entry: symptoms, how to detect, current mitigations (admission control, cache limits), and link to the compaction project.
SLO guidance: how tail latency SLOs incorporate fragmentation signals; alert thresholds for compaction regressions; escalation paths.
Dashboard spec: panels for fragmentation ratio, eviction rate, compaction CPU/GPU time, allocation failures, and p95/p99 per pool/region.
Operational runbook: triage checklist, safe runtime flag changes, pool-level mitigations, rollback steps, and when to page runtime oncall.
Postmortem: timeline, contributing factors (fragmentation + burst routing), customer impact, immediate mitigations, and follow-ups that seeded this project.
Linear project/umbrella issue: “KV cache compaction improvements” with milestones, owners, success metrics, and links to design/ADRs.
Instrumentation: add fragmentation ratio + allocation failure counters; include labels by region/pool/model family; define metric names and units.
Perf suite: add bursty-mix benchmark scenario; publish baseline results and regression gates.
Allocator refactor: introduce compaction-capable block map; ensure thread-safety and minimal overhead in fast path.
Eviction policy v1: define victim selection (age/tier/fairness); add tests for correctness and pathological cases.
Scheduler integration: add hooks for eviction pressure signals; ensure no starvation; document contract and invariants.
Compaction triggers: implement threshold-based triggers + per-interval budget; add safety guardrails to avoid thrash.
Feature flag + config: runtime flags for enabling compaction, setting budgets, and selecting eviction mode; default off.
Correctness tests: stress tests under concurrent decode/prefill; ensure no corruption across stream sync points.
Observability dashboards: implement the KV cache health dashboard in the observability pack; define alerts.
Canary plan: pick one hosted region + one dedicated pool; define success criteria and rollback triggers.
Rollout to 25% traffic: staged enablement and monitoring checklist; capture learnings and adjust thresholds.
Documentation: update profiling playbook + runbook + release notes; ensure oncall readiness.
Perf-canary: add new canary scenario to detect fragmentation-induced tails; integrate with release gating.
Follow-up: evaluate prefix-cache interactions (reuse vs eviction) and propose policy adjustments.
PR: Add KV cache fragmentation metrics + structured logging; includes metric naming, tags (region/pool/model), and unit tests.
PR: Refactor KV cache allocator into block map abstraction; prepares for compaction (no behavior change).
PR: Implement eviction policy v1 (victim selection + fairness constraints); adds simulator tests.
PR: Compaction engine (move blocks + update pointers/metadata); adds synchronization strategy and safety checks.
PR: Scheduler integration—introduce ‘cache pressure’ signal and backpressure coordination; updates scheduling heuristics.
PR: Feature flag + config plumbing for compaction/eviction modes; default off; adds runtime config docs in-code.
PR: Add regression tests for bursty traffic + mixed lengths; reproduces fragmentation tail behavior pre-fix.
PR: Optimize compaction fast path to reduce overhead; introduces compaction budget enforcement.
PR: Fix rare race in compaction vs decode stream sync; adds stress test and incident reference.
PR: Add benchmark scenario for fragmentation ratio and burst tails; publishes baseline tables and artifacts.
PR: Add perf-canary check for compaction-enabled runtime; gating on p99 and allocator failure rate.
PR: Add dashboard panels + alerts for KV cache health (fragmentation, eviction rate, compaction cost) with recommended thresholds.
Thread: runtime engineers coordinating design review for compaction approach; questions about pointer stability, stream sync, and worst-case overhead.
Thread: ADR discussion—debate block size and whether to allow moves; includes tradeoffs for kernel address calculations.
Thread: perf baseline results shared; identifies which workload mixes trigger the worst fragmentation; links to benchmark-lab run.
Thread: SRE asks for proposed alerting/rollback signals for canary; negotiates thresholds and paging strategy.
Thread: incident coordination during a burst tail latency event; notes about allocator failures and immediate mitigations (flag changes / pool routing).
Thread: oncall handoff—what to watch overnight during compaction canary; dashboards and safe toggles.
Thread: release engineering coordinating runtime build that includes compaction flag; discusses rollout sequencing and backport considerations.
Thread: debugging a race found in stress tests; shares logs, minimal reproducer config, and assigns fix owner.
Thread: review feedback on PR series; discussion about test coverage and perf regressions in median latency.
Thread: canary results after 24h—p99 improvement vs one regression in a specific model/pool; decides to tune budgets.
Thread: PMs ask whether improvements will change customer-visible latency SLOs; coordinates comms for Dedicated accounts.
Working doc: early brainstorming, alternative approaches (slab allocator vs segmented pages), open questions, and links to Slack threads/PRs.
Spreadsheet: baseline fragmentation ratio and tail latency across scenarios/regions/models; includes charts and a ‘regression gate’ tab.
Doc: back-of-the-envelope cost model for compaction (bytes moved, expected GPU copy cost, sync overhead) and proposed budgets.
Checklist: step-by-step canary enablement, dashboards to watch, rollback conditions, and communications plan.
Slide deck: design review for compaction/eviction; diagrams of allocator states, trigger policy, and expected impact.
Slides: dashboard mockups and panel definitions; proposed alerts and examples of ‘bad’ patterns.
Customer support ticket: Dedicated customer reports bursty p99 latency spikes; investigation points to KV cache fragmentation; links to incident + planned compaction rollout.
Customer support ticket: Hosted API timeouts during high load; Support requests mitigation guidance; SRE references runbook and interim tuning.
Customer support ticket: OOM events correlated with long-context traffic; includes logs and environment details; escalated to runtime team.
Internal support ticket: request to add new runtime metrics to central telemetry schema and ensure retention in observability pipeline.
Fireflies transcript: technical deep dive with an enterprise prospect evaluating Dedicated; discussion focuses on tail latency, memory fragmentation, and upcoming compaction strategy.
Fireflies transcript: PoC check-in where customer shares burst traffic traces; Redwood team explains canary plan and what metrics will improve.
Email thread: internal escalation after a customer-facing latency event; aligns Runtime + SRE on priority, staffing, and timeline; includes links to SUP ticket and postmortem.
Email thread: infra/reliability leadership review of canary risk and rollback plan; requests specific alert thresholds and oncall coverage.
Email thread: product comms planning for key accounts; sets expectations on when tail latency improvements will land and how to describe the change (no breaking behavior).
HubSpot deal note: enterprise evaluation where tail latency stability is a decision criterion; logs technical objections and links to the technical deep dive call.
HubSpot support/escalation summary: account timeline, impact statement, promised follow-ups, and mapping to Jira SUP tickets + rollout milestones.
